_comment: Mutation-scores the validation suite itself (research doc step 7): mutants that survive mark assertions the graph/step/report tests do not actually pin. Scope = the execution spine (engine, step runner/graph, step wirings, stage logic) plus the provenance builders. Run: make mutation (repo root) or npx stryker run (web/). `break` is set a few points under the measured score so regressions bite without flaking; re-measure before raising it.
_ignoreStatic_comment: Static mutants (module-load wiring literals: unit-id strings, wireUnit name args, steps arrays) are false-survivors under the vitest runner: the mutated init runs during the untracked initial import and is module-cached, so the active-mutant gate never sees it. Proven empirically 2026-07-20 — stepGraph.test.ts asserts the exact literal values (e.g. intervalCleaningWiring.unit === 'interval_cleaning') and the corresponding mutants still survived. 45 such false-survivors vs 516 statics the fresh-process path does kill; ignoring statics trades those detections away for an honest denominator.
_thresholds_comment: Measured 2026-07-20 after the survivor burn-down (two verify-by-injection rounds, +160 tests): 96.22% with ignoreStatic (1,835 detected / 72 survived / 0 no-coverage). The 72 survivors are documented-equivalent mutants (proofs in the burn-down session notes: comparator sign-only sorts, boundary ties selecting equal values, subsumed guards, coercion identities). break=93 bites on regression without flaking on mutant-set drift; re-measure before raising.
